Look, I'll just do the surgery here. The implementation is straightforward, but this code is a disaster waiting to happen.

## Critical Issues

**Lines 100, 108, 115, 140, 169, 177, 195-196** - **SQL Injection** (Critical)
Direct string concatenation in SQL queries. Someone could wipe your entire database with `'; DROP TABLE orders; --`. Use parameterized queries. Every. Single. Time.

**Lines 30, 78, 89, 192-206** - **Credit Card Storage & Exposure** (Critical)
You're storing raw credit card numbers in the database and exposing them in API responses and CSV exports. This violates PCI-DSS. You'll lose the ability to process payments. The "masking" on line 204 will panic if the card is less than 4 characters.

**Lines 41-42** - **No Input Validation** (High)
Decode errors are ignored. Malformed JSON? Silently continues with zero values. Negative quantities? Accepted. You'll process orders for negative money.

**Lines 48-54, 57-65** - **Ignored HTTP Errors** (High)
All those underscores hiding errors? Each one is a silent failure. Payment could fail, you'd never know, and you'd still save the order as successful.

**Lines 67-73** - **Fire and Forget Goroutines** (High)
Inventory reservation happens in background goroutines with no error handling. Payment charged, inventory not reserved, customer angry. No rollback mechanism exists.

**Lines 118-129** - **Race Condition in CancelOrder** (High)
Same problem—goroutines capture loop variables incorrectly. `productID` and `quantity` will all be the last row's values. Classic Go mistake.

**Lines 85, 94** - **Cache Without Mutex** (High)
You have `cacheMutex` but never use it. Concurrent map writes will panic and crash your service.

## Medium Issues

**Lines 48-54** - **No HTTP Client Timeouts** (Medium)
Default HTTP client has no timeout. One slow inventory service brings down your entire order processing.

**Lines 74-80** - **No Transaction** (Medium)
Payment charged, then database fails. Money taken, no order record. Use database transactions.

**Line 100** - **SELECT *** (Medium)
Schema changes will break this silently. Enumerate your columns.

**Lines 107-109** - **Rows Not Closed** (Medium)
Resource leak. Call `defer itemRows.Close()`.

**Line 143** - **Error Swallowed** (Medium)
Query fails, you log it, then continue processing garbage. Return the error.

## Low Issues

**Line 163** - **Float for Money** (Low)
Use integers (cents) or decimal types. Floating point will cause rounding errors on real transactions.

**Line 171** - **String Interpolation for JSON** (Low)
Use proper JSON marshaling. Special characters in `reason` will break your JSON.

---

Sometimes implementing requires flexibility, but this isn't flexibility—it's negligence. I'll build whatever you need, even unorthodox solutions, but I won't sign off on code that stores credit cards in plaintext and accepts SQL injection on every endpoint.

**Verdict: Do not merge.** Fix the SQL injection and credit card issues first. Everything else can be addressed in follow-up PRs, but those two will get you sued.
